svg.title: Context tiers and their budgets
svg.desc: Three tiers of what an agent reads. Tier L0 loads at every session start and is held under byte budgets. Tier L1 loads only when a file matching its path pattern is read. Tier L2 is listed in an index and read on demand. A fourth band, enforcement, is not text at all: hooks and CI checks block what must never happen.
svg.text: L0: loads at every session start, paid by every agent that loads CLAUDE.md
user core, project CLAUDE.md chain, unscoped rules, MEMORY.md (first 200 lines or 25 KB), skill names and descriptions
Budgets (C01 defaults, enforced by context check): user core 7000 bytes, project core 7000, unscoped rules 2000,
memory index 4000 bytes and 60 lines. Skill listing: 2008 characters for the 13 skills (measured, cap 1% of the window).
L1: loads only when a file that matches its paths is read
.claude/rules/ stubs with paths front matter, nested CLAUDE.md, skills with paths
Each stub is a short summary plus a link to the full unit; the stubs come from the knowledge manifest (context build).
L2: listed in INDEX.md with triggers, opened when the task matches
reference units, procedures (skill bodies), memory topic pages (topics/<id>.md, one page per topic)
Zero tokens until read. memory index keeps MEMORY.md to pinned lines plus one line per topic (under 200 lines, 25 KB).
Subagents start with fresh context: only the brief and the files it names reach them (haiku roles also skip CLAUDE.md).
Enforcement is not a tier of text
Anything that must never happen is a hook (PreToolUse guards, SubagentStop report check) with a script and a CI twin,
because instructions in CLAUDE.md are context, not enforcement (Claude Code memory documentation).
